_anchors.canvas.w: 48 = 3x the 16px cell of the Stardew idiom (BACKLOG round 1, control). Height comes out of the idiom, it is not an independent knob this round.
_anchors.canvas.originY: canvas.h / 2 - 2, so the fixture's 12px legs land inside the frame
_anchors.tones.perMaterial: the opening conviction of BACKLOG round 1: 4, knob range 3-6
_anchors.frames.walk: 4, anchored to the Stardew idiom, which is the control
_anchors.light.x: unit vector from the upper left (-0.6, -0.8), the pixel-art default; the anchor every future shading rule is derived against
_anchors.light.curve: 1 = linear. Off here and only here: the fixture holds the baseline hash still, and pow(u,1/1) is the identity, so this file's render is byte-for-byte what it was.
_anchors.light.y: the y half of light.x's unit vector; y grows down, so -0.8 is above
_anchors.outline.enabled: on, and it is a knob: the 'ink' question held for the human in BACKLOG turns on it
_anchors.outline.inner: off here and only here: the fixture is what the baseline hash is taken from, and this knob is a behaviour change. The probe samples are where it is exercised.
_anchors.outline.rim: off. The silhouette edge by value instead of line - a rim on the lit side, an occlusion edge on the shadow side. This is the knob the silhouette round is comparing against outline.enabled, and it is off in every sample that predates the round.
_anchors.outline.material: the palette ramp the outline draws from; its darkest tone
_anchors.body.scale: 1 = identity; the grammar is authored at 1:1 with canvas pixels
_anchors.gait.swing: asin(6/12) in turns = 0.0805 -> 0.08: a foot stride of half the 12px leg length
_anchors.texture.speckle: 0 = the injected RNG is never called. Sample C (high-budget idiom) is where it turns on.
_anchors.playback.msPerFrame: 125 ms = 8 fps. frames.walk (4) at 8 fps is a 0.5 s cycle, which is the Stardew control's walk; the '~1 s' sample of CLAUDE.md section 1 is the clip, and it loops twice inside it. The core never reads this number - it is the page's tick, and the first number a timing round will move.
_anchors.playback.scale: 4 = integer nearest-neighbour. 48 px at x4 is a 192 px cell: readable at arm's length, and no fractional scale to judge through.
_anchors.light.z: the lamp sits slightly on the viewer's side. Backfilled when the depth solver arrived: at -1 every surface faces the light and the body flattens to one tone, at 0 the light grazes and the far half goes black. -0.35 puts the centre of a mass around two thirds up its ramp and still leaves the lit and shadow edges at the two ends.
_anchors.gait.depth: canvas.w / 8 = 6 px. Backfilled with the depth solver; no track in this sample uses the z channel, so it is inert here. It is the body's half-width rather than 0 so that it already means something the day a depth track is added.
_anchors.shadow.steps: 8 px, and it is measured rather than chosen: a sweep at 6, 10, 16 and 24 returns the same shadow area from 6 onward. Past a few pixels the ray has left the body and there is nothing more to block it. 8 keeps a small margin over the saturation point.
_anchors.shadow.bias: 0.4 px of depth. Measured both ways: at 0.75 the shadow covers 5.3% of the body and at 0.4 it covers 8.7%. The cost of the lower value is surface acne, which fragments the tone regions - the findings channel measured that cost at 230 regions to 239 on the tree, which is small enough to pay.
_anchors.shadow.strength: 1 ramp step. On a five-tone ramp that is a fifth of the whole range, which is a readable value drop with a hard edge - the shape the ink verdict of 15/08 selected. 0 disables the pass.
